item.create_regex_filter.regex_filter.to: _Matches items_ and _fluids_ whose _name_ (in any _language_) or _mod ID_ matches a _regular expression_. Can be used in _Filter Slots_ of Create's Components
create_regex_filter.gui.language.hint: Click to use your game language
create_regex_filter.gui.target.item_name: The pattern is matched against the item's name as shown in its tooltip, in the language selected next to the pattern. Renamed items use their custom name.
create_regex_filter.gui.target.mod_id.de: The pattern is matched against the ID of the mod that adds the item, for example minecraft or create.
create_regex_filter.gui.mode.allow.descr: Items matching the pattern pass, everything else is rejected.
create_regex_filter.gui.mode.deny.descri: Items matching the pattern are rejected, everything else passes.
create_regex_filter.gui.ignore_case.desc: When on, upper and lower case letters match each other: iron matches Iron Ingot. Replaces (?i), which is not supported.
create_regex_filter.gui.help.find: The pattern can match _anywhere_ in the text: use _^_ and _$_ to match all of it.
create_regex_filter.gui.help.case: Upper and lower case are told apart unless _Ignore Case_ (the _Aa_ button) is on.
create_regex_filter.gui.help.syntax: _RE2_ syntax: like Java's, without back-references and lookarounds.
create_regex_filter.gui.sample.descripti: Put an item here to check whether the filter lets it through. It is not saved on the filter.
create_regex_filter.gui.sample.name: Name: %s
